correctness.rationale: The normalized matrix state yields exact Gram-matrix purity and the rectangle decomposition. Uniform q-root Fourier orthogonality gives the expectation criterion at each phase site. In the cubic expansion: identical plaquettes contribute 1/4 only at q=3; exactly two identical have a unique phase site in the third and vanish; distinct triple terms survive precisely when three plaquettes form a 2-row/3-column or 3-row/2-column triangle, T choices, six permutations, with 8 surviving orientations at q2 versus two at q>=3. This establishes μ3 for all integer U,V>=2 and q>=2 or continuous phase distribution, with endpoints U=V=2 included. Same algebra gives established variance and standardized skewness. Separately, exact monomial-conservation enumerations tested 30 grid/alphabet settings and 72,706 completely enumerated finite state configurations, with Gram-matrix identity checks. These tests support but do not replace the universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact third cumulant is the first finite-size non-Gaussian correction for fixed-cut purity in the Hadamard-Butson ensembles whose mean, variance, and Gaussian numerical approximations are analyzed by Trotta et al. Its quantized q=3 resonance is invisible in the variance and distinguishes phase alphabets at the level of skewness. The complete all-dimension third-order law and sharp balanced asymptotics answer a natural physical statistics question rather than an arbitrary parameter sample; no downstream theorem or full distribution is claimed.
